scope: Every numbered theorem, proposition, lemma, definition, example, remark and algorithm of paper/main.tex and its included fragments is indexed in TeX order, with its page in paper/main.pdf, and eight supporting anchors (equations and Appendix A) are listed. Every field of the nine components of the Lean proposition KE02.CoreCertificate, and every field of KE02.Algorithm2Outcome, is mapped to the declarations that prove it. Each entry states its coverage: formalized in full, formalized scalar part only, exact finite cross-check only, or written proof only. Where a Lean statement uses Lemma 2.1, convexity of F and the secant bounds (9) are explicit premises; Lemma 2.1 itself is not formalized.

lean.scope: KE02.CoreCertificate has no hypotheses; each of its nine components is a structure of universally quantified statements with all premises explicit. Where the paper uses Lemma 2.1 for the spectral function, the Lean statements take an arbitrary function F with convexity and, where needed, the secant bounds (9) as premises. No spectral theory, matrix gap statement, oracle as an algorithm, cost or complexity bound is formalized.

numbered_results.title: Main theorem
numbered_results.covered: The scalar facts its proof uses about Algorithm 2, for every n ≥ 1, δ > 0, convex F with (9) and every reply function that meets the requested accuracies: the run returns t with [t - h, t + h] ⊆ [0, δ/n], so 0 ≤ t and nt ≤ δ; it makes at most 3 + 8K requests, all at points of [0, δ/n] with accuracies δ/(2^16 K n^4) < ε ≤ δ/(512n), hence ε < 1 for δ < 1/2; K is found by doubling; h ≤ δ/(2n) < 1 and h^2/(2^20 n^4) > 2^-34 δ^2 n^-12, which Proposition 3.1 turns into the gap bound; and the second inequality of (5).
numbered_results.not_covered: ‖D‖_2 ≤ δ and the gap bound as matrix statements, which need Proposition 3.1 and spectral theory; that F is the spectral function of T + tX, and Lemma 2.1; that the oracle of Lemma 4.3 and Appendix A produces replies meeting the accuracy premise; the model of computation and every operation count, including O(n[1 + log(n/δ)]^3).

numbered_results.title: Local gap certificate
numbered_results.covered: The scalar steps of the proof: 0 < h ≤ 1 gives 0 < γ ≤ 1/(256n^2) for γ = h^2/(2^20 n^4); the quotient in (27) is (13); (28) at t - h, t and t + h gives S_h(t) ≥ S_h^aux(t) - (4n/h)N for arbitrary real functions; 1 - 384n^2 √γ/h = 5/8 > 1/2; and the complete scalar chain from S^aux ≥ 1, N ≤ 96n√γ and the three bounds |F - G| ≤ nN to S_h(t) > 1/2.

numbered_results.title: Improved selection of a separating perturbation
numbered_results.covered: Algorithm 2 is the Lean transcript KE02.alg2Run for an arbitrary reply function, line by line: K least with 2^K ≥ 16n^3 and found by doubling, θ = 1/(4K), the three initial requests and the seven plus one requests of each refinement with their tolerances, the selection with ties to the left and the stopping test. Under the accuracy premise and for convex F with (9), the run executes a return statement at the first successful test, so the last line is not reached, after exactly 3 + 8j requests for j refinements.
numbered_results.not_covered: Convexity of the spectral function and (9), from Lemma 2.1, are premises; that the replies come from the oracle of Lemma 4.3 is not formalized.

numbered_results.title: Contraction of endpoint slope variation
numbered_results.covered: (35) for every convex F, 0 < θ ≤ 1/4 and h > 0, with the sum inequality of the proof; the estimate error 1/64 for the tolerance 2θh'/256; and (36), for one refinement with arbitrary replies and at every performed refinement of every run of Algorithm 2 whose replies meet the requested accuracies.
numbered_results.not_covered: Convexity of the spectral function F, Lemma 2.1, which enters as a premise.

numbered_results.title: Improved constructive spectral separation
numbered_results.covered: For every n ≥ 1, δ > 0, convex F with (9) and every reply function that meets the requested accuracies: termination after at most K = ⌈log_2(16n^3)⌉ refinements; (37), that is S_h(t) < 1/2, [t - h, t + h] ⊆ [0, δ/n] and h > δ/(128n^4); at most 3 + 8K evaluations, all at points of [0, δ/n]; nested windows and the potential bounds of the proof; the stopping-test error θ/32 ≤ 1/128 and 1/8 + 1/128 + 1/64 < 1/2; Bernoulli's inequality and L_K > δ/(64n^4); h ≤ δ/(2n) < 1, 0 ≤ t and nt ≤ δ; and the scalar inequality h^2/(2^20 n^4) > 2^-34 δ^2 n^-12 used for (38). The premises are satisfiable.
numbered_results.not_covered: (38) itself, which applies Proposition 3.1, and ‖D‖_2 = nt; that F is the spectral function, whose convexity and secant bounds (9) are Lemma 2.1.

numbered_results.title: Improvement over the basic selector
numbered_results.covered: No Lean declaration or exact check is assigned; the quantities it compares are those of Lemma 4.2 and Theorems 4.1 and 4.2.
numbered_results.not_covered: The comparison of the two selectors.

numbered_results.title: Spectral-function oracle
numbered_results.covered: The algebra and arithmetic of Appendix A that the oracle uses: the recurrence ends in det(zI + 2I + A); k Graeffe steps give ∏(z + r_j^(2^k)); p_j ≤ e_j ≤ 2^n p_j; k least with 2^k η ≥ 8n and found by doubling, with 4n/R ≤ η/2; and, for roots in (0, 4), the index-wise matching with error η/2 in every eigenvalue and weighted error at most ε. The bound n(n+1)η/2 in the remark after the lemma is also formalized.
numbered_results.not_covered: The lemma as a statement about an algorithm: that the procedure applied to F(t) = Σ_j jλ_j(T + tX) meets the accuracy ε, P(z) = ∏(z + r_j) (spectral theorem), the complex Hermitian c_i, balanced product trees, Fourier transforms and roots of unity, the arithmetic model and the cost O(n[1 + log(n/ε)]^2).

supporting_steps.label: app:oracle
supporting_steps.title: The spectral-function oracle: algebraic details
supporting_steps.covered: The determinant of a tridiagonal matrix over any commutative ring R : Type is the continuant, and for every real tridiagonal A the recurrence ends in det(zI + 2I + A), with c_i = A_(i,i+1)^2 for symmetric A; the even/odd split, one Graeffe step and its k-th iterate ∏(z + r_j^(2^k)) for all real roots; the e_j as elementary symmetric sums, positive, with p_j ≤ e_j ≤ C(n,j) p_j ≤ 2^n p_j; the R-th root as k square roots; 2^x - 1 ≤ x on [0, 1]; |r̂_j - r_j| ≤ 4n/R; k least with Rη ≥ 8n and found by doubling R from 1, so that 8n/η ≤ R < 16n/η and 4n/R ≤ η/2; η = ε/Σj and the index-wise matching λ̂_j = r̂_(n+1-j) - 2 with weighted error at most ε.
supporting_steps.not_covered: P(z) = ∏(z + r_j) and r_j ∈ (0, 4), which need the spectral theorem and are premises in Lean; the complex Hermitian c_i = (Re A_(i,i+1))^2 + (Im A_(i,i+1))^2, checked exactly on instances only; balanced product trees, Fourier transforms and roots of unity; the operation counts; and the coefficient growth e_j ≤ 2^n 4^(nR).
